Key benefits & who needs one Why corporate customers buy webstores

Key benefits

What the store does for your customer
Save time
Standard
Automated
Reduce administrative overhead with self-serve ordering. No more email back-and-forth on every apparel request.
Brand consistency
Standard
Locked-in
Maintain professional appearance — only approved logos, colors, and product styles appear in the catalog.
Employee satisfaction
Standard
Self-serve
Easy 24/7 access to company-approved apparel. Great for new-hire onboarding and uniform replacement.
Reporting
Standard
InkSoft admin
Track orders, top-selling items, revenue by date, supporter contact info. CSV export on request.
Who needs a webstore? Companies experiencing: excessive time spent on apparel requests · difficulty tracking supplies · inconsistent inventory · complex employee uniform programs · challenges with exchanges/returns · a need for streamlined new-hire onboarding.
Store types & pricing Open/Close vs On-Demand

Two store models

Pick the one that matches your customer's ordering pattern
Open/Close
+$2.00 per item sold
Seasonal or campaign-driven. Staff opens the store for a defined window (1–6 weeks typical), collects orders, closes it, runs the production batch. Best for: team fundraisers, back-to-school drives, new-hire onboarding, one-time gear orders.
On-Demand
+$6.00 per item sold
Year-round, always open. Customer controls open/close. Each order ships individually. Best for: ongoing uniform programs, customer-service give-aways, employee perks, anytime ordering convenience.
Setup fee
One-time
$300.00 flat
Covers store design, branding, product catalog, payment integration, testing, and launch support. Same fee regardless of store type.
Logo digitization
$100 per logo
One-time fee to convert artwork into stitchable .DST embroidery files. Waived if customer has approved designs on file with NWCA. Typical: 1–3 logos per store.
Annual minimum
$2,000 /year sales
If the store doesn't generate $2K in supporter orders over 12 months, customer is billed the shortfall. Most active corporate stores easily clear this.
How each item is priced: Take our standard 1–7 tier left-chest embroidery price for the garment (garment + a left-chest logo) and add the per-item fee for the store type ($6 on-demand · $2 open/close). That total is what the supporter pays at checkout — the fee covers webstore handling and one-at-a-time production.
Example (on-demand): a polo at $30.00 embroidered (1–7 tier) → $36.00/item on the store.
Setup timeline: 1–2 weeks from artwork approval to live store  ·  Platform: InkSoft (industry-standard custom apparel e-commerce)  ·  Payment: Credit cards via Payrix · gift certs supported
Best practices & track record How to set up for success

Setup best practices

• Start with 4–6 different garment styles — too many overwhelms supporters
• Limit colors to 1–3 per style for simplicity (and faster production)
• Keep logo placement consistent across items
• Begin with core items — polos, t-shirts, jackets — before specialty
• Plan for seasonal needs upfront (fall jackets, summer tees)
• Designate a single point of contact at the customer for orders/questions

Live stores we operate

18+ corporate webstores running on InkSoft today

Store types & pricing Open/Close vs On-Demand

Two store models

Pick the one that matches your customer's ordering pattern
Open/Close
+$2.00 per item sold
Seasonal or campaign-driven. Staff opens the store for a defined window (1–6 weeks typical), collects orders, closes it, runs the production batch. Best for: team fundraisers, back-to-school drives, new-hire onboarding, one-time gear orders.
On-Demand
+$6.00 per item sold
Year-round, always open. Customer controls open/close. Each order ships individually. Best for: ongoing uniform programs, customer-service give-aways, employee perks, anytime ordering convenience.
Setup fee
One-time
$300.00 flat
Covers store design, branding, product catalog, payment integration, testing, and launch support. Same fee regardless of store type.
Logo digitization
$100 per logo
One-time fee to convert artwork into stitchable .DST embroidery files. Waived if customer has approved designs on file with NWCA. Typical: 1–3 logos per store.
Annual minimum
$2,000 /year sales
If the store doesn't generate $2K in supporter orders over 12 months, customer is billed the shortfall. Most active corporate stores easily clear this.
How each item is priced: Take our standard 1–7 tier left-chest embroidery price for the garment (garment + a left-chest logo) and add the per-item fee for the store type ($6 on-demand · $2 open/close). That total is what the supporter pays at checkout — the fee covers webstore handling and one-at-a-time production.
Example (on-demand): a polo at $30.00 embroidered (1–7 tier) → $36.00/item on the store.

Best practices & track record How to set up for success

Setup best practices

• Start with 4–6 different garment styles — too many overwhelms supporters
• Limit colors to 1–3 per style for simplicity (and faster production)
• Keep logo placement consistent across items
• Begin with core items — polos, t-shirts, jackets — before specialty
• Plan for seasonal needs upfront (fall jackets, summer tees)
• Designate a single point of contact at the customer for orders/questions
